item.title: PM moves motion to table Constitution Bill report at a later date and to replace Prof. Prasad on Committee with Nand

item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister, Sitiveni Rabuka has moved a motion in Parliament to table the report of the Special Parliamentary Committee on the Constitution Amendment Bill at a later date.

fijivillage News has received confirmation that the report and the third reading of the Constitution Amendment Bill is expected at a later date but before the end of the current parliament's term which is 24th December this year.

Rabuka also moved for independent MP, Sachida Nand to replace National Federation Party Leader and Government MP, Professor Biman Prasad on the Special Parliamentary Committee.

While responding to Rabuka, Professor Prasad maintains more time is needed for constitutional changes to be made, and for the Constitution Bill to come back after the general elections.

Professor Prasad withdrew from the Parliamentary Committee over the weekend.

Leader of Opposition, Inia Seruiratu says they agree that more time is needed and they will continue to be on the Committee as they represent the people.

Seruiratu says they are already being questioned and things are being said on the social media that they have been offered diplomatic positions to support the Bill.

He stresses that this is not the case, and they are on the committee for the people.

SODELPA Leader and Minister for Education, Aseri Radrodro stresses that SODELPA wants more time for consultations for the people and the Bill not to be rushed to a final parliamentary vote.

Radrodro also highlighted that even provinces like Naitasiri hardly had any consultation.

item.title: Families on Cikobia and Naqelelevu Islands receive emergency water assistance amid El Niño conditions
item.description: Families on Cikobia and Naqelelevu Islands in the Northern Division have received emergency water assistance as Fiji continues to experience the effects of El Niño. Approximately 55,200 litres of water were delivered to Naqelelevu Island through emergency water carting operations carried out by the government vessel MLC Vatulawa. The National Disaster Risk Management Office says the vessel resumed
item.content:encoded:
Families on Cikobia and Naqelelevu Islands in the Northern Division have received emergency water assistance as Fiji continues to experience the effects of El Niño. Approximately 55,200 litres of water were delivered to Naqelelevu Island through emergency water carting operations carried out by the government vessel MLC Vatulawa.

The National Disaster Risk Management Office says the vessel resumed its operations over the weekend after refuelling at Malau Port, completing water deliveries to the remaining villages requiring assistance before proceeding to Naqelelevu.

At Naqelelevu, the water was successfully pumped ashore to support the community's needs.

The operation was coordinated by the NDRMO, under the Ministry of Rural and Maritime Development and Disaster Management, in collaboration with the Ministry of Public Works, Meteorological Services and Transport, the Water Authority of Fiji and the Office of the Commissioner Northern Division.

With dry conditions continuing, the NDRMO is urging households and communities to store water early and prepare for possible shortages.

Communities are encouraged to use clean, covered containers to store water, identify alternative water sources, conserve supplies and prioritise water for drinking, cooking and essential household needs.

The NDRMO says assistance to remote and maritime communities may take time to reach affected areas, and is urging people to prepare before their water supplies are depleted.

item.title: Truck driver arrested after suspected marijuana found at Narain Jetty raid
item.description: A truck driver has been arrested after police discovered a bag containing parcels of dried leaves and branches believed to be marijuana during a raid at Narain Jetty. Police say the raid was conducted last Friday night by a team from Totogo Operations, the Dog Unit and the Fiji Detector Dog Unit.
item.content:encoded:
A truck driver has been arrested after police discovered a bag containing parcels of dried leaves and branches believed to be marijuana during a raid at Narain Jetty.

Police say the raid was conducted last Friday night by a team from Totogo Operations, the Dog Unit and the Fiji Detector Dog Unit.

During the operation, K9 Herb indicated the possible presence of illicit drugs on a truck.

A subsequent search led to the discovery of a bag containing the suspected drugs.

The driver was arrested and taken into custody.

Police say the seized substances have been sent for testing as investigations continue.

item.title: Disaster teams to activate within 72 hours before potential disaster
item.description: Disaster response teams will be activated within 72 hours before a potential disaster, with provincial and district teams preparing communities directly in the projected path and coordinating resources based on the severity of the expected impact. This was highlighted by Provincial Administrator in Lomaiviti, Ravuama Nagatalevu during the National Disaster Risk Management Awareness Week – National
item.content:encoded:
Disaster response teams will be activated within 72 hours before a potential disaster, with provincial and district teams preparing communities directly in the projected path and coordinating resources based on the severity of the expected impact.

This was highlighted by Provincial Administrator in Lomaiviti, Ravuama Nagatalevu during the National Disaster Risk Management Awareness Week – National SIMEX 26, being held at Novotel in Lami.

Nagatalevu says preparedness work is carried out throughout the year, and the province does not usually follow the five-day activation period, instead activating its response within 72 hours before a potential disaster.

He says once a disaster track map is available, the first step is to follow up with Heads of Departments through the Divisional Commissioner and convene a meeting with relevant stakeholders.

Communities directly in the projected path will then be informed and prepared, while provincial and district disaster teams will be activated through the Commissioner’s Office to coordinate work on the ground.

Nagatalevu says response teams will be placed on standby with a skeleton crew within the 72-hour period.

Additional resources may be requested from other Heads of Departments at district and provincial level, or through the Commissioner’s team, depending on the severity of the expected impact.

He says the National Disaster Management Office also provides advice and funding to support response operations.

Meanwhile, Director of the National Disaster Risk Management Office, Napolioni Boseiwaqa, says the office will inform the National Disaster Control once the readiness trigger is met.

Boseiwaqa says an inter-cluster meeting will then be convened to review planned interventions with all relevant clusters.

Divisional offices will also be briefed on the planned interventions so they can coordinate the response on the ground, while other relevant agencies will be informed where possible.

The National SIMEX 26 exercise brings together disaster management officials, government agencies, emergency services and humanitarian partners to strengthen preparedness, test emergency coordination and practise decision-making during a disaster.

The programme includes sessions on national emergency response arrangements, inter-agency collaboration, tsunami response, anticipatory action and regional and international assistance.

The tabletop exercise also allows decision-makers to work through simulated disaster scenarios, including declaring a national state of disaster, coordinating the initial response and requesting regional and international assistance .

The exercise comes ahead of the 2026–2027 tropical cyclone season, which began yesterday.
